primary_comparison.scope: unchanged-input, human-adjudicated, hierarchy-aware point-comparable development slice
primary_comparison.interpretation: A same-input stochastic rerun improved this four-window slice because W4 changed from free_throw_made to the human-supported free_throw_miss. W1 remained wrong. The sample is too small to claim generalized model improvement or an architecture gain.

exact_subtype_check.scope: same four unchanged-input windows, excluding generic missed_field_goal hierarchy credit

window_2.summary: The action-complete clip recovered the reviewed steal and made two-pointer. Turnover and assist remain unadjudicated.

window_6.summary: The revised clip recovered the first reviewed missed two-pointer. It also produced a rejected turnover and assigned the rebound to the wrong team/sequence. The second miss and offensive rebound are label-supported but still lack audited point timestamps.
window_6.naive_label_time_warning: A label-and-time-only scorer can incorrectly award the defensive rebound prediction despite contradictory team/evidence semantics. Evidence-aware adjudication is required.

taxonomy_only_observation.window_7: The model used the desired generic made_field_goal label, but the reviewed timestamp remains approximate and its evidence still inferred two points from the scoreboard, contrary to the prompt. It is not included in the primary point metric.

limitations: W0 was not reviewed and was not run.
W2 and W6 use revised action-complete media and therefore have no same-input cached control.
W2 assist and turnover remain unadjudicated.
W6 second-miss and offensive-rebound point times remain unresolved.
W7 reviewed event time is approximate.
This run evaluates a tiny development slice and does not use the sealed holdout.
